name: Script compile, execute and unload
description: Covers execute_script, with and without compileOnly, and unload_script: clean, repeated and failing compiles with the line numbers they report, a script's own enum, unqualified Object, an internal type, iterator methods and auto-properties, types declared by execute_code (named, missing a member, declared twice, and still there after an unload), first runs, reruns of the same and an edited source with their static state, unload by other case, a Harmony patch removed by an unload by other case, of a name never loaded and after unloading, args of every JSON type, a MonoBehaviour with Update, a coroutine, a Harmony patch through ScriptContext.Harmony, a class-only script and a script naming its types, two files with one name, the second refused, Main() and Unload() throwing, a generic method with a lambda, mod types, a Main() looping past its 15s budget, stopped and left loaded, one whose loop catches every exception, stopped too, a Main() asleep past the budget and its 2s grace, reported still running, an execute_code queued behind it told what holds the main thread, an unload, an execute_code and a script that cannot start within their start budgets while a frame is held, an Unload() asleep past the budget whose teardown finishes once it returns, and a looping Unload() stopped with the teardown finished, ISO date strings in args, foreach over Dictionary Keys, Values and SortedDictionary, an edited script replaced while it uses a type execute_code declared, and a script declaring enum-typed constants, public and private, whose method and public constant execute_code names. It also covers an enum of an unloaded script no longer refused, an enum's name read as a member of another script's type, two scripts declaring one type, the second refused, Main(string[]) and overloaded Main and Unload, a script patching its own method, refused without taking the game down, every other route to a script-compiled method's body refused the same way (PatchAll, execute_code patching its own and a script's method, a script patching execute_code's, a reverse patch, GetOriginalInstructions, GetCurrentInstructions, HasMethodBody, GetMethodBody on a method, a constructor and a generic instance) while the same calls on a game or library method still answer, input naming Harmony or GetMethodBody refused when the guard is recorded as not installed, a component added to an object the script does not track, destroyed by the unload, and nameof. Several steps hold the game's main thread for 11 to 30 seconds; the holds that must outlast an unload or a Main() start wait until that action is queued, and the steps after them wait until the hold is in force. Its first step unloads every lifecycle script, patch and object an earlier failed run left behind; its last step checks nothing is left. Its cleanup runs the first step again whatever ended the steps, so no lifecycle script, patch or object outlives a failed run.
